notes: NUMBERS CONFIRMED TO ALL PRINTED DIGITS, but the inferential sentence is only conditionally supported. (1) Every number reproduces: 0.924586/1.062490/2.417880 vs claimed 0.925/1.062/2.418; the two independent floor methods agree (sigma 2.8437 matched-pairs vs 2.8330 moment decomposition). (2) The floor is NOT a measurement of bond-level reference heterogeneity: chemical forensics on the 1002 tol=0.1 pairs shows 0 pairs share both the same parent molecule and the same fragment set, 1000/1002 are DIFFERENT molecules, and only 4 fragment pairs repeat anywhere in the benchmark (n=2 each, experimental spread 1.0-3.9). The sd of dE therefore mixes reference noise with real structural/chemical differences, so 2.2689 is an UPPER bound on the oracle MAE; using robust scales on the same pairs gives 1.589 (ratios 1.32/1.52/3.45) and a median-|dE| floor gives 0.95 (ratios 2.21/2.54/5.77). The 'at or below floor' reading for quantum is an artifact of the Gaussian MAE conversion applied to a dE distribution that is strongly non-Gaussian (excess kurtosis 3.19, skew 0.81, Shapiro p=1.2e-20 at tol=0.1; top 5% of pairs carry 49% of the variance, 54 pairs exceed 8 kcal/mol). (3) Even keeping the Gaussian conversion, quantum is only at/below the floor for tol>=0.02; at exact quantum matches (tol=0, n=54 pairs) the floor is 2.002 and the quantum ratio is 1.048 (above floor). (4) The ratio framing hides a unit error: MAE does not add in quadrature, so 'MAE less than the floor MAE' does not imply zero channel error. The workstream's own method B implies a positive quantum-vs-truth sigma of 1.02 (P>0 = 0.989) and learned-vs-truth sigma of 2.00 (P>0 = 1.0), with P(sigma_L > sigma_Q) = 0.9995 - i.e. both channels ARE separable from a perfect estimator and from each other on that decomposition, contradicting the plain reading of 'cannot be separated from a perfect estimator at this sample size'. (5) The reference conclusion is robust: its ratio is 2.42 (CI95 [2.24, 3.42]) and 1.00 of bootstrap floors lie below its MAE, so 'genuinely worse' is safe. (6) Secondary caveats: 124 duplicate parent molecules mean the 543 rows are not independent (molecule-clustered CIs are ~10% wider but do not change the ranking); rounding granularity is coarse (reference values all 1 dp, quantum/learned 2 dp, only 284/494/479/290 distinct values for E/Q/L/R, 82 exact-integer experimental values); the ratios are stable across the 331 train / 212 non-train split (quantum 0.908/0.943, learned 0.877/1.289, reference 2.437/2.386). (7) The claim-5 instruction ('implement BOTH methods') and claim-11 instruction are boilerplate from other claim files; both methods were implemented anyway (they agree), and the ~165 check shows no naive pooled formula can produce 165 - the correct pooled within-molecule SD is 9.9654; 165.2623 is sqrt(weighted mean of variance-squared), a squaring slip in output/analysis/ws5_het.py line 24.
